comment: Logical element names: the original's CSS selector (and the child holding the text, when not the element, or the attribute naming an icon button) and the Swift accessibilityIdentifier. 'first' compares only the top-left match; 'text' also compares font size, weight and color; 'geometry: false' names an element only for steps to act on (click, expect), and it is not compared. Steps pick one of several matches by 'text' (the text child's text, an input's value, a pop-up's chosen item, or the 'textAttribute'; on the Swift side the accessibility label) or 'index' (top to bottom, then left to right). The toolbar's items are system items since P5-24 (D-015, D-016): the system places them, so they are named for steps and not compared, and of the customize elements only the panel is left (on the Swift side the system's sheet, named by AutomationTags). The » menu is the system's: no step opens it. 'toolbar menu' is what Sort, Theme, View Options and the Settings app menu stand in as. 'frame' says how much of a frame compares when the two sides' boxes differ around the same text: 'center' (a tight text box against a text field's, with its inset) or 'origin' (a box as wide as its text against one as wide as its row) or 'top' (as 'origin', against a text field that is also inset); the text style still compares.
